versions: 2.7 ∪ 3.x (through 3.13 syntax: match, PEP 695 type parameters and type aliases, except*, parenthesized with-items)

oracles.tool: tools/py-oracle/check.py under python3 (stdin batch, compile(src, path, 'exec'))
oracles.horizon_note: 3.12 rejects syntax newer than itself: PEP 758 (3.14 parenthesis-free multi-except) appears in one black fixture and is booked as noise here; it becomes a gap the day the oracle is bumped, and the bump gets its own before/after sweep.

oracles.tool: tools/py-oracle/check2.py under python2 (stdin batch, compile(src, path, 'exec'); the script is written in the py2/py3 common subset)
oracles.version: CPython 2.7.18, built from source (Ubuntu 24.04 ships no python2 package)
oracles.role: REQUIRED second leg of the union: every file python3 rejects is re-judged, and a file is valid if either accepts. The driver errors loudly if python2 is missing — a py3-only sweep books every py2-only file as noise, which silently hides the py2 half's gaps. Adding this leg surfaced 4 real gap files the py3-only sweep had mis-filed as noise.
oracles.battery: test/negative-oracle/py3/ (print statement, backticks, 0777, except-comma) verified live: python3 rejects all four, python2 accepts all four. test/negative-oracle/py2/ (f-string, nonlocal, walrus) verified live in the reverse direction. The battery caught its own bad fixture on first run: bare `nonlocal x` with no enclosing binding is a SyntaxError in py3 as well, so the fixture gained the enclosing function it needed.
oracles.bug_found_by_widening: The wider corpus crashed the py2 leg: a file with a NUL byte makes py2's compile() raise TypeError where py3 raises ValueError, and check2.py caught only the latter, so the oracle died instead of returning a verdict. A NUL in the source is a VERDICT (the bytes were read fine, they are just not python), not an oracle failure, so both are now caught. The loud-failure discipline worked exactly as designed — the sweep aborted rather than silently booking every python2 file as noise.

corpus.source: top-1000 PyPI packages by download rank (hugovk top-pypi-packages), sdists only; 951 of 1000 publish one
corpus.blind_to: python2-only code (modern PyPI sdists are effectively py3-only, so the py2 half of the union leans entirely on the corpus tests and batteries); notebooks; scripts without .py extension

sweep.oracle_note: adjudicated by the two-leg union oracle (CPython 3.12.3 + 2.7.18).
sweep.noise_note: noise verified by sampling: deliberately-broken test fixtures (jedi completion corpora, ruff/black invalid-syntax fixtures), templating files, and one PEP 758 (py3.14) black fixture — see oracle horizon_note
sweep.note: widened from the top-300 (46,466 files). Gap COUNT rose 13 -> 29 while the gap RATE fell 0.028% -> 0.021%; every family was already ledgered, and 24 of the 29 are ruff's parser test fixtures.

corpus.mutation_falsification: the same corpus swept against the grammar with while_statement deleted from _loop reports 3,661 gap files (vs 13); with star_pattern deleted from the match sequence rule it reports 17. The pipeline can say non-zero for both old and new rules, so 13 is a measurement.

known_gaps.construct: PEP 701 f-string edges (same-quote nesting, multiline interpolations opened at line end, \{ escapes)
py3 keywords as py2 identifiers (bare `nonlocal`, bare `await` — ruff parser fixtures)
known_gaps.note: the declared hard-keyword deviation, measured: 2 fixture files in 46,466, zero incidence in real library code

known_gaps.construct: parenthesized kwarg name `f((a)=1)`, valid <=3.7 and in py2
walrus/format-spec collision f"{num:=.2Uf}" (`:=` lexes as one token; CPython special-cases this in its tokenizer)
formatter test fixtures with deliberate edge layout (ruff/black `else:\` backslash-continuation, inline-if + comment interleavings)

deviations.what: py2 chevron print `print >> f, x` takes the expression reading (a tuple whose head is a right-shift) — it is valid py3 syntax too, and the union prefers the py3 reading whenever both parse (print_statement carries prec.dynamic(-1))

keywords that were identifiers in some version (True/False/None in py2, async/await before 3.7) are hard keywords here; `True = 5` (py2-valid) does not parse. Soft-keyword machinery exists for print/exec/match/case/type, which carry real corpus weight; the others measured no corpus incidence

`x = 1; if y: pass` (invalid in every version) is accepted when it ends the file: the zero-width NEWLINE the scanner hands out at EOF satisfies the line wrapper the inline suite already consumed. One negative-corpus candidate removed for it; fix wants a smarter EOF rule
inconsistent partial dedents (`if a:` at 0, body at 8, next line at 4) parse; CPython's tokenizer raises IndentationError. The scanner dedents to the nearest enclosing level

roles_note: 18 of 22 table-tier terms are threaded. Omitted: _type (python annotations are ordinary expressions — the vocabulary's own position), _modifier (python has no named modifier nodes yet; async/await are anonymous), _control_flow (unthreadable here: a supertype's members enter every position that references it, and clauses/jump-vs-branch positions are construct-specific — see the uncategorised reasons in roles.json). _clause MOVED to the facet tier in vocabulary 0.2.0 on exactly this evidence, gathered independently in python, rust and typescript; _control_flow remains the open candidate.
patterns_note: match patterns are a dedicated sub-grammar (PEP 634), not the expression rules. The shapes reuse the destructuring node names by alias — `(tuple_pattern)`, `(list_pattern)`, `(star_pattern)` mean the same thing in `a, b = x` and in `case (a, b)` — but they are NOT threaded through the `_pattern` supertype, and that is a measured decision rather than an oversight: python's destructuring and match positions admit different member sets (`x[0]` and `*rest` destructure but do not match; `Point(x=0)` and `{'k': v}` match but do not destructure), and a supertype's members enter every position that references it. Routing them through `_pattern` made `a, Point(x=0) = z` parse, which CPython rejects. This is the `_clause` law in a second place; rust does not hit it because its `let` and `match` patterns are one set. Consequence: `(_pattern)` covers destructuring positions here, and match patterns are reached by their shared concrete names.
